title: Greeks Bake Cakes for a Wish-Granting Saint
text:
• Thousands of pilgrims gathered at the Church of St. Fanourios in Ilion, Greece, with their baked offerings.
• The pilgrims were seeking solace for different forms of loss, including misplaced keys, estranged partners, and courage to face ordeals.
• Priests blessed the cakes of the supplicants, who then shared them with their fellow churchgoers for the feast of St. Fanourios.
• The feast culminates on Thursday, which is the day of St. Fanourios.
• Maria Chanioti, 66, has attended services dedicated to the patron saint of lost-and-found since her youth.
• Chanioti prepared her cake with fresh-squeezed orange juice and a pinch of nutmeg, in front of an icon of the saint and a simple vigil candle.
• Wishes conveyed to Fanourios go beyond mere custom, and each year's petition is held in earnest and usually not shared even with loved ones.
• Orthodox saints are regarded as spiritual companions – models of bravery and faith who channel prayer and provide protection.
• Saint Fanourios is known as “The Revealer" and is the patron saint of Rhodes, the Greek island where an icon depicting his suffering as a Christian martyr was discovered.
• The Church of St. Fanourios offers a recipe for the cake – called Fanouropita – which includes 4 cups self-rising flour, 1 tsp. cinnamon, 1 cup vegetable oil, and 1 cup orange juice.
• Father Nikolaos Vlavianos greeted parishioners and blessed their cakes at the Church of St. Fanourios on Wednesday night.
• Most people keep their wishes private, though Father Nikolaos has heard everything from illness and bankruptcy to parking woes and soccer slumps.
summary: They were seeking solace for different forms of loss: misplaced keys, an estranged partner, courage still needed to face an ordeal, and more. He helps people,” Chanioti said in her godparents' kitchen a few blocks from the Church of St. Fanourios, while she beat the cake's ingredients with a whisk. She prepared her cake as her family always has: with fresh-squeezed orange juice and a pinch of nutmeg, in front of an icon of the saint and a simple vigil candle.
